full_query: How am I supposed to put ointment on my nipple if it's pierced

shared_context.topic: applying ointment to a pierced nipple

sentences: When caring for a nipple piercing, it's essential to follow proper hygiene and aftercare techniques to promote healing and minimize the risk of complications
To apply ointment to a nipple piercing, follow these steps
Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and warm water before touching the piercing
Clean the piercing with a saline solution (1/4 teaspoon of sea salt in 8 ounces of warm water) to remove any debris or bacteria
Pat the area dry with a clean towel
Apply a small amount of fragrance-free, non-comedogenic ointment (e.g., Bacitracin or Neosporin) directly to the piercing, avoiding the jewelry
Gently rotate the jewelry to ensure the ointment is evenly distributed
When choosing an ointment, select one that is fragrance-free and non-comedogenic to minimize the risk of irritation
Avoid using petroleum-based products, such as Vaseline, as they can slow healing and cause skin irritation
It's also essential to follow a regular aftercare routine, which may include cleaning the piercing 2-3 times a day and applying ointment as needed
If you experience any signs of infection, such as redness, swelling, or discharge, seek medical attention immediately
